description: Exploit the PMADDUBSW and PMADDWD multiply-accumulate instructions to pack four 6-bit decoded values into three output bytes using only two instructions, replacing the naive 9-instruction shift/mask/or sequence. This treats the 4-to-3 byte packing as a linear algebra problem over integers.
mathematical_formalization: Input: [00dddddd|00cccccc|00bbbbbb|00aaaaaa]. Step 1: PMADDUBSW(input, [0x01,0x40,0x01,0x40,...]) = [0000ccccccdddddd|0000aaaaaabbbbbb]. Step 2: PMADDWD(result, [0x0001,0x1000,...]) = [00000000aaaaaabbbbbbccccccdddddd]. Total: 2 multiply-add ops.
analogical_connections: DSP: FIR filter where tap coefficients perform bit-position routing
Linear algebra: matrix-vector multiply where the matrix encodes bit-permutation
Codec design: quantization step in JPEG where multiply-add reorders DCT coefficients
implementation_hypothesis: For AVX-512, use VPMADDUBSW (zmm) + VPMADDWD (zmm) to pack 64 decoded 6-bit values into 48 output bytes per iteration. Follow with VPERMB to compact the 48 useful bytes.
experiment_seed: Compare cycles/byte of multiply-add packing vs naive shift-or packing on Zen4 and Sapphire Rapids. Verify correctness with all 2^24 possible 4-char inputs.
